BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft vs Buyer Playbook

**Basis:** Seller counsel's SPA update and Disclosure Letter, reviewed against the Wattlebridge playbook. The seller's "market standard," "settled," "agreed," and "FINAL" labels are assertions, not authority, so I have not treated them as reasons to accept any position. No fallback is recommended as acceptable because none has been authorised. Figures are as stated in the seller documents and are not independently verified. Legal review by NSW counsel is recommended before any position goes to the seller.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price, AUD 4,800,000, for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** Start at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% / AUD 4.8M figure is a conditional fallback that requires prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. None has been given.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; counter at 25%.
- **Reason:** We cannot concede the fallback without Amelia Frost's written authority.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000, with recovery only of the excess.
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, with the seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; counter at AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 first-dollar.
- **Reason:** The seller's terms are five times our thresholds and excess-only, which materially cuts recovery.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months from Completion, applied to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval. Fundamental and Title claims sit in their own regime.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; counter at 24 months.
- **Reason:** The "all Claims" wording would wrongly pull Title and Fundamental claims into the general period.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental / Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and buyer-knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; restore a separate regime.
- **Reason:** Merging the regimes is the hidden general-regime override the playbook prohibits.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** Cl 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature." No carve-out appears.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. This cannot be waived.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; insert the carve-out.
- **Reason:** As drafted, the limitation wording would capture fraud, and the playbook says no one may waive the carve-out.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (including DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the general disclosure in 1.1 and 1.2.
- **Reason:** General disclosure would convert every data-room document into an exception to the warranties.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** Cl 8.3 bars claims for any matter the buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket exclusion. Any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and a reasonable-enquiry standard. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Delete cl 8.3; replace with a qualifier that meets the playbook test if needed.
- **Reason:** A "discoverable from the data room" test is a blanket buyer-knowledge bar.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours only; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The Disclosure Letter confirms no final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6M of FY26 revenue (~30%).
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours are insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; make effective consent plus evidence of satisfied conditions a pre-Completion condition.
- **Reason:** Consent-on-delivery with an endeavours-only obligation leaves roughly 30% of revenue exposed after we have paid.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2M outstanding, with a release "to be provided following Completion." The Disclosure Letter confirms the facility is unpaid and no discharge is included.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-Completion release; require payout and releases through the funds flow.
- **Reason:** The playbook requires direct repayment, and we have no approval for a post-Completion release.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow. The disclosure does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.
- **Buyer wants:** A specific line item or seller funding, including triggered on-costs. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Recommendation:** Require a specific funds-flow line or seller funding, including on-costs.
- **Reason:** Silent exclusion would leave at least AUD 420,000, plus on-costs, with the buyer after Completion.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and described as "adequate." DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, not bank-verified. DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer conditional on payment, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** A broadened indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 is not verified either way.
- **Recommendation:** Broaden the indemnity; verify SOW3 payment status before accepting the figure.
- **Reason:** A SOW3-only indemnity does not cover transfer risk beyond the stated amount.

**SPA-N-012: Export / privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter" not expected to be material (cl 4.6 and Schedule 6). The record refers to about 1,240 records, unknown access, undetermined notification status, and no loss stated.
- **Buyer wants:** Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. Preserve logs, investigate, and require updates.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept "not material"; require log preservation, investigation and regular updates, and reserve our position on specific protection.
- **Reason:** The materiality conclusion is the seller's characterisation and the investigation is still open.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** AUD 330,000 aggregate, described as ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Assess the three renewals (DD-008 and DD-011). No automatic debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** Assess whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable or accrued; do not accept the "ordinary course" label; make no price adjustment yet.
- **Reason:** The characterisation is asserted rather than evidenced, and the playbook bars automatic debt treatment.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime," and all limitations apply to all Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories kept separate, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the merged regime.
- **Reason:** Merging categories creates the override the playbook prohibits.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the DD-012 share register, which records Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100%. The Disclosure Letter says the buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** Require independent title, encumbrance and authority verification before accepting the title position.
- **Reason:** The seller's own register cannot independently prove title.

**SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Terms remain open. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Recommendation:** Keep open; do not accept the general-regime settlement.
- **Reason:** The playbook treats these terms as unresolved, and "settled" is the seller's assertion.

---

**Cross-cutting points**
- The seller's preamble claims the positions were "settled at principal level" and are "not intended to be re-opened." Nothing in our file shows that, and under playbook 0.4 and 6.3 it does not bind us. Any movement on caps, time limits or Riverlark must go through Amelia Frost's written authority.
- Items that need action before the next turn: Bluefen consent evidence (N-008), the Riverlark payout figure (N-009), the bonus funds-flow line (N-010), the SOW3 payment status (N-011), the incident update (N-012), and independent title evidence (N-015).
